item.title: Remote work after five years
item.summary: A long essay on how remote work changed management.
item.text:
Remote work changed how teams plan their week, and the change has outlasted the reasons that first caused it. Managers who once measured presence now have to measure outcomes, and many of them say they were never taught how. The companies that adapted fastest were not the ones with the best tools but the ones that already wrote things down. Writing forces a decision to be stated, and a stated decision can be questioned by someone who was not in the room. There is a cost: people new to a team learn less by overhearing, and the people who used to teach by accident no longer do. Some firms answer with fixed office days, others with a week together every quarter, and neither has clear evidence behind it yet. What the surveys agree on is narrower than the headlines: most people want a choice, and few want the same choice every week. The longer view is that the office was a habit before it was a policy, and habits change more slowly than rules.

item.title: Appeal court: late deposit protection is not a lesser breach
item.summary: An appeal ruling that late protection of a tenancy deposit is penalised like no protection.
item.text:
The tenant paid a deposit of six weeks rent when the tenancy began and the landlord did not place it in an approved scheme within the thirty days the statute allows. The landlord argued that the lateness was a technical slip that caused the tenant no loss, since the money was protected before the tenancy ended. The court below accepted that argument and awarded the lowest penalty the statute permits. On appeal the question was whether a court may treat late protection as a lesser kind of breach than no protection at all. The panel held that the statute draws no such line, and that the penalty turns on the culpability of the landlord and not on the loss to the tenant. It noted that a professional landlord with several properties is expected to know the rules, while a first-time landlord letting a single flat may deserve more leniency. The decision does not disturb the earlier rule that a notice seeking possession is invalid while the deposit is unprotected. Commentators expect the ruling to raise the awards made in the county courts, where the lowest multiple had become the habit.

Giving the lead judgment, Lady Justice Okonkwo said: "Parliament chose a penalty and not compensation. A landlord who protects late has still broken the duty." The other two members of the panel agreed.

item.title: Five versus ten days of amoxicillin for childhood pneumonia
item.summary: A trial abstract finding five days of amoxicillin no worse than ten for children with pneumonia treated at home.
item.text:
Background: Whether a shorter course of antibiotics is enough for children with uncomplicated pneumonia treated at home has been uncertain.
Methods: We randomly assigned 824 children aged 6 months to 5 years to five days or ten days of amoxicillin. The primary outcome was treatment failure by day 28, defined as a further antibiotic prescription for a respiratory infection.
Results: Treatment failure occurred in 12.6% of the five-day group and 12.4% of the ten-day group, a difference of 0.2 percentage points that met the margin for non-inferiority. Cough lasted a median of 12 days in both groups. Rash was reported less often with the shorter course.
Conclusions: Among children with pneumonia who can be treated at home, five days of amoxicillin was not inferior to ten days. A shorter course exposes children to less antibiotic and may be easier for families to complete.

item.title: debounce(fn, wait, options) | utilkit
item.summary: Reference for a function that holds a callback back until calls stop arriving.
item.text:
The function schedules the callback once the wait has passed without another call, which is what a search box or a resize handler usually wants. Each call cancels the timer set by the one before it, so only the last call in a burst runs. When the leading option is set, the first call of a burst runs at once and later calls are held back. The returned function keeps the arguments of the most recent call and the value of this from it. It is not the same as throttling, which lets one call through in every interval however many arrive. Remember to cancel a pending call when the component that owns it is removed, or the callback will run against a view that is gone.

Parameters

Name | Type | Meaning
fn | Function | The callback to hold back
wait | number | Milliseconds to wait, 0 by default
options.leading | boolean | Run on the first call of a burst

Example

input.addEventListener('input', save);

item.title: Python function for a loan repayment schedule
item.summary: A function that works out the monthly payment and total interest of a repayment loan.
item.text:
def amortise(principal, annual_rate, years):
    """Monthly payment and total interest for a repayment loan."""
    r = annual_rate / 12
    n = years * 12
    if r == 0:
        return principal / n, 0.0
    payment = principal * r / (1 - (1 + r) ** -n)
    total = payment * n
    return payment, total - principal


for rate in (0.0419, 0.0445):
    monthly, interest = amortise(250_000, rate, 25)
    print(f"{rate:.2%}: {monthly:,.0f} a month, {interest:,.0f} interest")

item.text: Notes on the school start time study. The district moved the first bell at its four high schools from 7:40 to 8:30 and followed the same students for two years. The researchers were careful about what they could and could not claim, because there was no control district and the change came in the same year as a new timetable. Even so, the direction of every measure was the same. Students slept 34 minutes longer on school nights, and they did not simply go to bed later, which is what sceptics had predicted. First-period absences fell by 15%, and the share of students who said they fell asleep in class at least once a week dropped from 31% to 19%. Grades moved very little, which the authors treat as honest evidence that sleep is not a quick route to better marks. Teachers reported calmer first lessons. Bus costs rose, since the routes could no longer be shared with the primary schools, and after-school sport finished in the dark for part of the winter. The board voted to keep the later start and to look again at the bus contract.

item.summary: 六家社区老年食堂的经营情况和老人的反馈。
item.text: 社区老年食堂调研小结。上个月我们走访了城东的六家社区老年食堂，和四十多位老人、十几位工作人员聊了聊。总体的感受是，老人对食堂的需要是真实的，尤其是独居和行动不便的那部分人，一顿热饭解决的不只是吃的问题，还有每天出门见人的理由。但食堂的日子并不好过。六家里有四家在亏损，一份午餐平均卖12元，成本却要16元左右，差额靠街道补贴和企业捐赠填上。每家每天的就餐人数大多在80人上下，周末会少一半。几位负责人都提到，人手是最大的难题，厨师留不住，志愿者也不稳定。老人这边抱怨最多的是菜太咸、太硬，以及送餐不准时。也有做得好的，比如和附近的小学合用厨房，把成本摊薄；还有一家请老人自己参与择菜和分餐，既省了人手，老人也愿意来。我们的建议是，补贴不要只按人头发，要和服务质量挂钩，同时鼓励食堂对周边居民开放，用市场价的午餐补贴老人餐。

item.text: Notes from the planning call about the neighbourhood tool library. Everyone agrees the idea is good and that the hard part is the boring part. The church hall will give us the old cloakroom for nothing as long as we are out of the way on Sundays. Shelving and a decent lock come to about £600, which the residents association can cover. Insurance is the thing nobody had thought about. Lending someone a ladder is not the same as lending them a book, and the hall will want to see a policy before we open. Priya knows someone who runs a library of things in Leeds and will ask how they handle it. We talked for a while about deposits and decided against them, because they keep away exactly the people who need to borrow a drill. Opening would be Saturday mornings to start with, two volunteers at a time. Still open: who holds the keys, what we do about power tools, and whether we charge a membership.

item.title: Three days on the ridge with Tom
item.summary: A hut-to-hut walk, the long second day and the last morning.
item.text: Three days on the ridge with Tom, written up on the train home so I do not forget. We started late on the first day because the bus from the valley only runs twice, and reached the first hut as the light went, soaked from the knees down. The warden had kept soup for us. The second day was the long one: 19 km along the crest with the cloud lifting and closing all morning, and then a descent that my knees are still complaining about. We saw two ibex above the tarn and nobody else until four in the afternoon. Tom carried the stove the whole way and never once mentioned it. On the last morning we were up at five to watch the sun come over the far wall of the valley, and it was so quiet that we could hear the stream a long way below. Total climb over the three days was 2,400 m according to his watch. At the top of the last pass he said, "Same time next year, and you carry the stove." I said yes before I had thought about it.

item.text: 今天带小满去做两岁的体检。早上出门的时候她还不肯穿外套，在门口哭了好一会儿，最后是抱着她的小兔子才肯走。到了医院人很多，排了快一个小时。量身高的时候她站得笔直，好像知道这是件要紧的事。身高88厘米，体重12.5公斤，医生说都在正常范围里，比半年前长了不少。查牙齿的时候她怎么都不肯张嘴，医生拿了一个小镜子给她玩，才看了一眼，说已经出了十六颗。医生问平时吃饭怎么样，我说挑食，不爱吃青菜。医生说不用太着急，换着花样多试几次就好。回家的路上她在车里睡着了，醒来第一句话是：“妈妈，医生的镜子可以带回家吗？”我和她爸爸都笑了。晚上给爷爷奶奶打电话，她抢着说自己长高了。

item.title: Reading notes, chapter four of the book on how cities age. The argum…

item.text: Reading notes, chapter four of the book on how cities age. The argument of the chapter is that the buildings a city cannot afford to replace are the ones that keep it alive, because cheap old space is where new things start. A bookshop, a rehearsal room or a repair business cannot pay the rent on a new block, and a district made only of new blocks has room for banks and chain restaurants and little else. The line I copied out: "New ideas must use old buildings." She is not sentimental about it. Old buildings matter for their low overheads and not for their charm, and a district of nothing but old buildings is usually a district in trouble. What a street needs is a mixture of ages, so that high-yield and low-yield uses can sit side by side. To take into the essay: the point about overheads and not charm; the mixture of ages as the real requirement; and the warning that clearing a block at once removes the cheap space for a generation.

item.title: My first marathon
item.summary: The day of the race, from the cold start to the finish.
item.text: Ran it. I am writing this on the sofa with my feet in a washing-up bowl. The start was colder than forecast and I wore the bin bag until the gun, like everyone else. The first half felt easy, which the coach had warned me about, and I held back as promised. The crowds on the bridge were three deep and somebody had a sign that said the end is near, which was not true. At thirty kilometres my left calf started to tighten and I walked through two water stations, eating the orange quarters a child was handing out. Mum and Ana were at the last corner with the dog. I do not remember the final straight at all. Finish time 4:12:37, and I was 6,804th, which I am told is the middle of the pack. I said at the line that I would never do it again and by the evening I was looking at the dates for next spring.

item.text: The trouble with measuring a teacher by test scores is not that the scores mean nothing. It is that once the measure decides who is paid and who is dismissed, people begin to work on the measure and stop working on the thing it was meant to show. A number that was a fair witness becomes a poor judge.

item.text: Economists like to say that there is no such thing as a free lunch, and most of the time they are right, but the phrase hides how unevenly the bill is shared. When a factory saves money by venting its waste into a river, the cost does not vanish. It lands on the people downstream, who pay in dirty water and never see an invoice. Costs of this kind are called externalities, and a great deal of politics is an argument about who should be made to carry them. The lunch was never free. It was only served at one table and charged to another.

item.text: How the newsletter got started, for the record. At first it was only a list of links I sent to four friends on Fridays. Then one of them forwarded it to her team, and by the summer strangers were replying with corrections, which I took as a sign that someone was reading. I never planned any of it, and every attempt to make it more professional has made it a little worse.
